analysis:
## 200-DMA flips to support, ETF tide turns — FOMC in four days

Saturday, June 13: Bitcoin rose 1.5% to $64,519 on a quiet weekend session following one of the most significant structural shifts of the past month. The price action itself was unremarkable — BTC tested the 200-DMA zone intraday (low $63,415), found a bid, and recovered to $64,519. But the context is anything but unremarkable: [all 13 US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net inflows on June 12, totalling $85M](https://coingape.com/markets/bitcoin-price-prediction-btc-chart-flashes-bullish-signal-as-etf-inflows-return/) — the first net-positive day since May 15. That ended a 13-session outflow streak that drained $4.4B from the ecosystem. The SpaceX IPO rotation is over. The capital is available to return. Today's +1.5% on a Saturday is the early evidence that redeployment has begun.

## Technical analysis

**Trend read:** Recovering — BTC has carved a sequence of higher lows since the June 6 capitulation wick ($59,480), and today's session extended that sequence above the 200-DMA zone for the first time in this correction.

**The 200-DMA transition.** The 200-day moving average (approximately $63,500–$63,600) acted as a ceiling for three consecutive sessions: BTC tested it June 10, 11, and 12 without a convincing close above. On June 13, the dynamic changed. The session low of $63,415 dipped briefly below the MA, found a bid, and reversed more than $1,100 without a retest. Former resistance becoming intraday support is one of the most reliable bull-structure confirmations in technical analysis. That transition happened today. Whether it holds is the question FOMC will answer.

**Momentum.** RSI recovering from deeply oversold conditions at the June 5–6 trough toward neutral (estimated ~43–46 range). MACD histogram compressing toward a potential bullish cross. The eight-session pattern since June 5 is a textbook coiling recovery: lower-high volatility collapsing, higher lows building a base, energy accumulating for the next directional move. The primary trend since the $98,600 peak remains down. But the ETF inflow reversal and 200-DMA support flip are the early signals that this recovery can extend further than prior bounces in the corrective sequence.

**Volume — the critical caveat.** Saturday's Crypto.com exchange volume tracked at approximately 30% of weekday average: roughly 1,370 BTC ($88M) vs. 4,410 BTC ($280M) on Friday and 4,167 BTC ($265M) on Thursday. Total 24-hour spot volume was estimated near $9.8B vs. roughly $29B+ on recent weekdays. A 200-DMA break on 30% of normal volume is the classic low-conviction weekend extension — not the same as a volume-validated institutional breakout. The 200-DMA transition is real but structurally unconfirmed until Monday's ETF flow either extends the June 12 inflow or reverses it. That is the next data point that matters.

**★ Strongest resistance: $65,000 — FOMC re-risk trigger + options call cluster.**
This level concentrates three independent forces:
1. It was the stated BUY trigger from the prior session dossier — a daily close above $65K was the signal to move from HOLD to aggressive long.
2. Call open interest on Deribit clusters heavily at the $65K strike, meaning dealer delta-hedging creates a self-amplifying bid once price approaches from below.
3. It is a round number in a market where round-number psychology is real and measurable.
At $64,519, BTC is $481 (0.75%) below this level. If Monday ETF flows confirm the June 12 reversal, the path to $65K becomes nearly mechanical. A FOMC hold/neutral statement Wednesday with BTC at $64–65K is the short-squeeze setup of the year: SpaceX capital returns, ETF flows accelerate, and short sellers who positioned at the 200-DMA see the level flip and unwind.

**★ Strongest support: $63,500–$63,600 — the 200-DMA zone.**
Former three-session resistance, now confirmed as the intraday floor. The evidence: June 13 low of $63,415 absorbed the selling and reversed $1,100 without a retest of the low. A daily close below this zone before FOMC is the warning signal — it would mean the 200-DMA resistance-to-support flip has failed and the setup needs to be re-evaluated before the binary event.

**The June 27 max pain gravitational pull.** The June 27 quarterly options expiry carries approximately $8B in notional with max pain near $75,500. Max pain is not a mechanical price predictor, but when the notional is this large and spot is 17% below max pain, it describes a derivatives market that is structurally short delta above current levels and must hedge an upward move. If FOMC provides any cover on Wednesday, the pull toward $67–70K in the first post-FOMC window, and toward $75K by June 27, has real mechanics behind it — not just narrative. The June weekly max pain near $63,000 is the competing force through this week's expiry; those two dynamics resolve in opposite directions, with FOMC as the tie-breaker.

**Decision points:** A daily close above $65,000 on Tuesday or post-FOMC Wednesday is the aggressive-add signal. A daily close below $63,500 (200-DMA) before FOMC is the reduce-risk warning. The $59,480 June 6 wick is the hard stop — if that fails, $52–55K reopens and the bull thesis for this cycle is invalidated.
